## What the item text tells us

<!-- The -data chunk makes these objects for the text and the questions; the -prep chunk
     makes them again for the exercises, which learnr runs in a fresh environment. -->

```{r {{id}}-data, include = FALSE}
item_info <- lab$item_info
.tk_pars <- coef(mirt(resp, 1, itemtype = models[2], verbose = FALSE),
                 IRTpars = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)$items
difficulty <- data.frame(
  item = rownames(.tk_pars),
  b = rowMeans(.tk_pars[, grep("^b", colnames(.tk_pars)), drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))
.tk_feats <- mirtverse::item_features(item_info, id = "item")
.tk_cand <- c("words", "numbers", "sentences", "max_digits", "decimals", "negation",
              "grade", "option_words", "key_longest")
.tk_cand <- .tk_cand[vapply(.tk_cand, function(v) v %in% names(.tk_feats) &&
                              !anyNA(.tk_feats[[v]]) && stats::sd(.tk_feats[[v]]) > 0, logical(1))]
text_features <- utils::head(.tk_cand, max(1L, floor(nrow(item_info) / 8)))
```

```{r {{id}}-prep, include = FALSE}
item_info <- lab$item_info
.tk_pars <- coef(mirt(resp, 1, itemtype = models[2], verbose = FALSE),
                 IRTpars = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)$items
difficulty <- data.frame(
  item = rownames(.tk_pars),
  b = rowMeans(.tk_pars[, grep("^b", colnames(.tk_pars)), drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))
.tk_feats <- mirtverse::item_features(item_info, id = "item")
.tk_cand <- c("words", "numbers", "sentences", "max_digits", "decimals", "negation",
              "grade", "option_words", "key_longest")
.tk_cand <- .tk_cand[vapply(.tk_cand, function(v) v %in% names(.tk_feats) &&
                              !anyNA(.tk_feats[[v]]) && stats::sd(.tk_feats[[v]]) > 0, logical(1))]
text_features <- utils::head(.tk_cand, max(1L, floor(nrow(item_info) / 8)))
```

### Features of the wording

Every item's text exists before anyone answers it. If features of the
wording (its length, the numbers in it, its options) predict how hard an
item turns out to be, item writers can aim new items at the difficulty a
test needs, and reviewers can look first at items that are much harder or
easier than their wording suggests.

`item_info` holds the text of `r nrow(item_info)` of the items.
`item_features()` measures each one: Its length in words and sentences, a
reading grade, the numbers it uses, its options and how similar it is to
the most similar other item. Save the result as `feats`.

```{r {{id}}-feats, exercise = TRUE, exercise.setup = "{{id}}-prep"}
feats <- item_features(item_info, id = "item")
feats
```

```{r {{id}}-feats-check}
lab_need(exists("feats") && is.data.frame(feats) && nrow(feats) == nrow(item_info),
         "Save the result of item_features(item_info, id = \"item\") as `feats`.")
.i <- which.max(feats$similarity)
sprintf("The most similar pair is %s and %s (similarity %.2f).", feats$id[.i], feats$nearest[.i],
        feats$similarity[.i])
```

```{r {{id}}-q-dup}
.tk_i <- which.max(.tk_feats$similarity)
.tk_dup <- .tk_feats$similarity[.tk_i] >= 0.85
question_radio(
  "Does any pair of items look like near-duplicates (a similarity of .85 or more)?",
  answer("Yes", correct = .tk_dup,
         message = if (.tk_dup) sprintf("Right: %s and %s have a similarity of %.2f. Near-duplicates on one form cue each other; check whether both should stay.", .tk_feats$id[.tk_i], .tk_feats$nearest[.tk_i], .tk_feats$similarity[.tk_i]) else "Look at the largest value in the `similarity` column."),
  answer("No", correct = !.tk_dup,
         message = if (!.tk_dup) sprintf("Right: The most similar pair, %s and %s, has a similarity of only %.2f.", .tk_feats$id[.tk_i], .tk_feats$nearest[.tk_i], .tk_feats$similarity[.tk_i]) else "Look at the largest value in the `similarity` column."),
  allow_retry = TRUE)
```

### Predicting difficulty from the text

`difficulty` holds each item's difficulty from the `r models[2]` model
`r if (lab$polytomous) "(the mean of its thresholds)" else ""`. Join it to
the features and ask `predict_difficulty()` how well a few features predict
it. It fits a linear logistic test model (LLTM), which says how much each
feature adds to difficulty, and a lasso, and it judges both by
cross-validation: Each item's difficulty is predicted by a model that never
saw that item. `text_features` holds the features used here:
`r paste(text_features, collapse = ", ")`.

```{r {{id}}-predict, exercise = TRUE, exercise.setup = "{{id}}-prep", exercise.lines = 8}
feats <- item_features(item_info, id = "item")
items <- merge(difficulty, feats, by.x = "item", by.y = "id")
m <- predict_difficulty(items, features = text_features, b = "b", id = "item",
                        methods = c("lltm", "lasso"))
m
```

```{r {{id}}-predict-check}
lab_need(exists("m") && inherits(m, "mv_difficulty"),
         "Save the result of predict_difficulty() as `m`.")
.best <- m$accuracy[which.max(m$accuracy$r2), ]
sprintf("The better model, the %s, explains %.0f%% of the variance in difficulty for items it did not see. tidy(m) shows what each feature adds.",
        c(lltm = "LLTM", lasso = "lasso", forest = "random forest")[[.best$method]], 100 * max(0, .best$r2))
```

```{r {{id}}-q-predict}
.tk_items <- merge(difficulty, .tk_feats, by.x = "item", by.y = "id")
.tk_m <- mirtverse::predict_difficulty(.tk_items, features = text_features, b = "b", id = "item",
                                       methods = c("lltm", "lasso"))
.tk_r2 <- max(.tk_m$accuracy$r2)
.tk_band <- if (.tk_r2 >= 0.5) 1L else if (.tk_r2 >= 0.2) 2L else 3L
.tk_why <- sprintf("The cross-validated R2 is %.2f.", .tk_r2)
question_radio(
  "How well do these features predict difficulty for items the model has not seen?",
  answer("Well: R2 of .50 or more. They could narrow the range of a new item's difficulty before field testing.",
         correct = .tk_band == 1L, message = .tk_why),
  answer("Moderately: R2 from .20 to .50. They help writers target difficulty, but every item still needs a field test.",
         correct = .tk_band == 2L, message = .tk_why),
  answer("Poorly: R2 below .20. The wording features used here say little about difficulty.",
         correct = .tk_band == 3L, message = .tk_why),
  allow_retry = TRUE)
```

```{r {{id}}-q-leak}
question_radio(
  "Someone adds the proportion of field-test examinees who answered each item correctly as a feature, and R2 jumps to .95. What happened?",
  answer("The feature was computed from the same responses as the difficulty, so it leaks the answer; the model cannot be used before a field test.",
         correct = TRUE,
         message = "Right. predict_difficulty() warns when a feature correlates this strongly with difficulty."),
  answer("The model finally found the feature that explains difficulty.",
         message = "A feature that is only known after the field test cannot predict a new item's difficulty before it."),
  answer("Cross-validation failed.",
         message = "Cross-validation worked; the feature itself already contains the field-test results."),
  allow_retry = TRUE, random_answer_order = TRUE)
```
